title: Require: downgrade guard
blurb: Streams live synthetic audio and canvas video across four tampered and intact signaling scenarios, using getStats() packet counters to verify InvalidAccessError rejection, clear-packet dropping, and silent negotiate fallback.
question: When a middlebox strips a=cryptex from an answer, does 'require' block the call via InvalidAccessError or drop clear RTP packets at the receiver while 'negotiate' silently falls back?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless with --enable-blink-features=RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy: honest signaling flowed ~415 packets; answer-stripped with receiver 'require' sent ~407 packets with 0 received; answer-stripped with offerer 'require' rejected with InvalidAccessError; answer-stripped with both 'negotiate' flowed ~417 packets in the clear. Unflagged flows all four in clear with explicit label.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (unflagged and --enable-blink-features=RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Under 'negotiate', stripping a=cryptex silently downgrades RTP headers to plaintext with no dedicated runtime state property on RTCPeerConnection or RTCRtpTransceiver
friction.repro: Run the 'Answer stripped, both negotiate' scenario; media flows normally (~417 packets) with unencrypted header extensions because webrtc-extensions PR #256 removed the per-transceiver read-only cryptex state signal.
friction.workaround: Parse both localDescription.sdp and remoteDescription.sdp for a=cryptex to detect whether header encryption was actually negotiated, or enforce 'require'.
